subject: Post-demo: BluePeak inference probes & hallucination/regression plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@bluepeak.com>, Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: BluePeak inference probes & hallucination/regression plan

Hi Ethan / Sophie,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the thorough questions on inference costs and quality tradeoffs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock scope for the probe POC: 

Summary of what BluePeak needs from us:
- Side-by-side quality and hallucination baseline vs the hyperscaler endpoint you mentioned on the call.
- Regression checks against your 200-domain prompt set and a conversational support set.
- Latency & cost measurements at realistic throughput (50–200 TPS burst).

What we propose (draft):
1) Run two competitive arms for 72 hours: Redwood prod profile vs Hyperscaler API (same prompts, same tokenization).
2) Metrics: hallucination rate (precision/recall on entity facts), semantic similarity vs ground truth, token-level latency p50/p95/p99, cost-per-1k-tokens.
3) Regression tests: daily diff on token-level distributions and hallucination delta; automated alert if hallucination delta > 3ppt for any domain.
4) Deliverables: side-by-side report, filtered example cases (false positives / hallucinations), and a shortlist of quantization/config knobs we recommend.

I attached the initial prompt set we used during the call (20280411-probe_prompt_set.csv) and the demo recording for reference (demo-recording-20280404.mp4).

Questions for you to confirm:
- Do you want us to include your internal KB documents for retrieval-context prompts? If so, please share 1–3 sample docs.
- Any legal/IT constraints for us hitting the hyperscaler endpoint from Redwood (IP allowlisting)?
- Target launch date for the POC results (we suggested 2 weeks on the call).

Next steps: if you confirm the scope we’ll spin up the runs and send a precise test matrix and expected timeline end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
(attachment: 20280411-probe_prompt_set.csv, demo-recording-20280404.mp4)

From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@bluepeak.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@bluepeak.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BluePeak inference probes & hallucination/regression plan

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. This looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications before we lock scope: 

1) Hallucination metric: can you outline the operational definition you’ll use? For our internal KPIs we typically track hallucination as any asserted entity-level fact not present in the provided context or KB. For conversational answers that require synthesis we allow a degree of summarize-but-cite behavior.

2) KB docs: yes — we’ll share three redacted product spec PDFs and a short internal FAQ (Sophie will push to your Drive link). We want retrieval-augmented queries included as a separate arm.

3) Hyperscaler endpoint: no special network allowlist needed; we’ll provide a service account key for their API and the relevant test account.

Timeline: 2 weeks is fine. Can you include a short A/B plan to compare hallucination-focused prompts vs generic prompts?

Also attaching a short example of our support prompts so you can seed the conversational set (attachment: bp_support_prompts_sample.txt).

—Ethan
Ethan Liu
Head of Product Integration | BluePeak Systems
ethan.liu@bluepeak.com
(attachment: bp_support_prompts_sample.txt)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BluePeak inference probes & hallucination/regression plan

Ethan / Rachel / Sophie — quick technical addendum on the test matrix and measurable definitions so the analytics team can script the runs: 

Operational definitions / test details:
- Hallucination: we’ll mark a response as a hallucination when it asserts an entity-level fact (P = person/place/number/date/product SKU) that does not appear in the combined (prompt + KB) context. We’ll surface both automated fuzzy matches (string/ner overlap) and manual review samples for edge cases.
- Semantic-quality: use embedding cosine vs reference answer (thresholds and distributions to be provided).
- Regression delta: daily comparison of hallucination-rate and mean token length per prompt bucket.

Test arms & config:
A) Redwood default serving profile (standard kv-cache, 8-bit quantized where applicable)
B) Redwood high-accuracy profile (higher precision kernels, slightly higher cost)
C) Hyperscaler API default config (we’ll match sampling/temp/topk where possible)
D) Retrieval-augmented variant (A + KB)

Load & sampling:
- Replay 10,000 prompt invocations per arm across your support + domain prompts, distributed over two 12-hour windows to catch burst variation.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and per-token cost with logs attached.

Deliverables & acceptance criteria:
- CSV export of per-prompt responses, hallucination boolean, confidence score, latency, token count.
- Example set of 50 failure cases per arm for manual triage.
- Passing: if Redwood hallucination delta <= 2ppt vs Hyperscaler on domain prompts and latency targets (p95 < 450ms) met, we mark quality OK for next step. Otherwise we recommend focused prompt engineering and quantization tradeoff changes.

I’ll have the infra team provision the sandboxes once Rachel confirms scope and we get the artifacts from BluePeak.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler-profiles.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: BluePeak inference probes & hallucination/regression plan

Ethan / Sophie — great, thanks for the quick replies and the sample prompts. Confirming scope and timeline below so we’re aligned: 

Scope confirmed:
- Arms: Redwood default (A), Redwood high-accuracy (B), Hyperscaler default (C), Redwood + KB retrieval (D).
- Prompt sets: BluePeak support prompts (provided), company-domain 200 prompts (provided), and the probe_prompt_set we shared.
- Metrics: hallucination (entity-level), semantic similarity, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-1k.

Timeline:
- 4/13: BluePeak uploads KB samples to Drive (Sophie) + shares hyperscaler test account details (Ethan).
- 4/14: Redwood spins sandboxes and starts scripted runs.
- 4/16 (EOD): Initial side-by-side report and CSV exports; we’ll schedule a 30-min review with your team on 4/17.

Action items assigned:
- BluePeak: share KB sample docs and service account key (due 4/13 EOD)
- Redwood (Ben): provision sandboxes and finalize test script (start 4/14)
- Redwood (Rachel): upload test matrix & HubSpot meeting invite (in progress) — link: https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/1234567/bluepeak-probe-review

If that looks good I’ll mark this in the deal record and send the meeting invite. Thanks — looking forward to getting the data back to you.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
